items.definition: A wide way leading from one place to another, especially one with a specially prepared surface which vehicles can use.
A railway locomotive, or a machine with moving parts that converts power into motion.
A colorless, transparent, odorless liquid that forms the seas, lakes, rivers, and rain and is the basis of the fluids of living organisms.
A flexible tube conveying water or other fluid from a source to where it is needed.
An opening, particularly one in a pipe, tube, or a part of the body.
An authoritative order given to a person or animal.
A person who carries a message or is employed to carry messages, letters, or parcels.
A yellow precious metal, valued especially for use in jewelry and decoration, and to guarantee the value of currencies.
A system of money in general use in a particular country.
A large plant-eating domesticated mammal with solid hoofs and a flowing mane and tail, used for riding and carrying loads.
A narrow valley between hills or mountains, typically with steep rocky walls and a stream running through it.
A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
A person who buys and sells goods or assets for others, especially on a stock exchange.
A room, set of rooms, or building used as a place for commercial, professional, or bureaucratic work.
A person who takes part in an undertaking with another or others, especially in a business with shared risks and profits.
A fast train, bus, or overnight delivery service that travels between a limited number of destinations.
A robber or outlaw belonging to a gang and typically operating in an isolated or lawless area.
A traveler on a public or private conveyance other than the driver, pilot, or crew.
A thing designed or used for inflicting bodily harm or physical damage.
A deep gorge, typically one with a river flowing through it, as found in North America.
A telegraphic instrument that prints stock prices, news, etc., onto a paper tape.
An area or arena in which commercial dealings are conducted, especially for stocks or commodities.
A person employed in an office or bank to keep records, file papers, or perform other administrative duties.
The capital raised by a business or corporation through the issue and subscription of shares.
A large amount of money or assets; or the success or failure that falls to anyone.
